pr_comments:
It might be possible to implement this in a more compact way by reusing `fun_bc_attr()` (in objfun.c): point to this function in the generator type info, then modify that function to check the type of self_in.  If self_in is a generator type then extract the `self->code_state.fun_bc` value, otherwise just use self_in as that value.

If that works and doesn't increase the code size by much then I'd also suggest not having an additional config option and putting this feature under the existing MICROPY_PY_FUNCTION_ATTRS config option.

> If self_in is a generator type then extract the self->code_state.fun_bc value, otherwise just use self_in as that value.

`mp_obj_gen_instance_t` is defined in `objgenerator.c`, how would you access the code state from `objfun.c` in this case?

It seems that this PR implements `__name__` for generator instances, rather than generating functions which what #3293 was reporting.  And support for `__name__` on generating functions was added in e2e22e3d7e29985579b2c91c639c71229422f349

issue_context.title: Generator function has no __name__ attribute
comments: It's a bit of a shame that there is code to print the generator name but not extract it in a programatic way (ie via `.__name__`).  The feature could be added almost for free by reusing the fun_bc_attr() function for normal functions, but there's one level of extra indirection that's needed to extract the name from a generator....

In b488a4a8480533a6a3c9468c2f8bd359c94d4d02 generating functions were optimised so they used the same structure as normal bytecode functions.  This made it possible to add support for `__name__` to generating functions very cheaply.  See e2e22e3d7e29985579b2c91c639c71229422f349

I think this now fixes the issue here.
